TL;DR

Welcome back to Dev Opportunity Radar.

This is a weekly series where I share opportunities, resources, communities, and interesting finds that I come across, with the goal of helping people discover things they might otherwise miss.

This week's edition features Develop for Good, MLH Global Hack Week: Agents, the OpenAI Student Collective, and Learning How to Learn, a free Coursera course that has helped millions of people become more effective learners.

If you're new to the series, you can now browse previous editions, search past opportunities, and explore Community Finds, Reader Updates, and Resources Worth Checking Out on the Dev Opportunity Radar website. I've also written a short post about why I built it. You'll find links to both at the end of this article.

If you've discovered something through the radar, I'd love to hear about it. Whether you applied to an opportunity, joined a community, completed a program, or found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd be happy to feature your experience in a future 💙 Reader Updates section (with your permission).

And if you've come across an opportunity, resource, community, program, or event that deserves more attention, feel free to share it in the comments.

📍 This Week's Opportunities

Here are a few opportunities I came across this week that I thought were worth sharing.

📌 Develop for Good Winter 2027 Student Volunteer Program

Who it's for: University students, bootcamp graduates, and recent graduates (with less than two years of full-time work experience) who want to gain real-world product, design, or engineering experience while contributing to nonprofit organizations. International students are welcome, and the program is fully remote.

What stands out: Develop for Good matches students with nonprofit organizations to work on real technology projects over a 16-week virtual program. Participants join cross-functional teams alongside designers, engineers, and product managers, receive mentorship from industry professionals, and build products that support causes like education, healthcare, sustainability, poverty alleviation, disaster relief, and more.

I wanted to include this because one of the biggest challenges early in your career is answering the question, "How do I get experience if every opportunity asks for experience?" Programs like this help bridge that gap. Unlike many volunteer programs, this one is intentionally structured to feel like working on a real product team. Instead of working on another tutorial or personal project, you get to collaborate with a real client, solve real problems, and build something that can become a meaningful portfolio piece.

Another thing I like is how closely the experience mirrors a real software team. Students work through project planning, stakeholder communication, technical collaboration, documentation, and product delivery over four months. Participants can also receive mentorship, recommendation letters, portfolio case studies, and opportunities to network with professionals during Demo Day. For eligible students from underserved and underrepresented backgrounds, the Develop for Good Fellows program also provides $1,536 unrestricted cash grants upon successful completion.

Program Duration: 16 weeks (Winter 2027 Batch)

Time Commitment: Approximately 5–10 hours per week

Format: Fully remote

Roles Available: Engineering, Design, Product Management, Technical Management, and Design Management

Who can apply: Applicants aged 18+ who are university students, bootcamp students, or recent graduates with less than two years of full-time work experience. International students are eligible.

Application Deadline: September 15, 2026

🔗 Learn More | 🔗 Apply

📌 MLH Global Hack Week: Agents

Who it's for: Students, beginners, aspiring developers, experienced engineers, and anyone interested in learning about AI agents through hands-on challenges. You don't need prior hackathon experience to participate, and the event is open to people around the world.

What stands out: Global Hack Week: Agents is a free, week-long online event hosted by Major League Hacking (MLH) that combines workshops, technical challenges, community activities, and project building around the theme of AI agents. Throughout the week, participants can attend live coding sessions, complete challenges at their own pace, earn points, connect with other builders on Discord, and learn directly from the MLH community.

I wanted to include this because learning about AI agents is becoming increasingly valuable, but it can be difficult to know where to start. This event lowers that barrier by combining guided workshops with practical challenges, making it approachable whether you're experimenting with agents for the first time or looking to build on your existing skills.

Another thing I like is that you don't have to commit to building a full hackathon project over a weekend. Instead, you can participate throughout the week, choose the challenges that interest you, attend live sessions, and learn alongside thousands of developers from around the world. It's a great way to build new skills, meet other developers, and stay motivated without the pressure of a traditional hackathon.

Event Dates: August 7–13, 2026

Format: Fully online

Cost: Free

Who can apply: Anyone, anywhere. All experience levels are welcome, including beginners and non-students. Participants aged 13+ may join with parental permission.

Registration: Open

🔗 Learn More & Register

📌 OpenAI Student Collective

Who it's for: Undergraduate students who enjoy building communities and are excited to help others learn how to use AI tools like ChatGPT and Codex. Students from all majors are encouraged to apply. The program is open to students studying in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, India, Japan, and South Korea.

What stands out: The OpenAI Student Collective is a new campus leadership program where students work in pairs to build AI communities at their universities. Campus Leads organize workshops, host weekly Studio Hours where students can build projects together, run campus showcases, and help create an environment where anyone curious about AI can learn and experiment.

I wanted to include this because AI communities on campus are growing quickly, but they often depend on a few students taking the initiative to bring people together. This program gives students the support, resources, and funding to create those spaces while helping others become more confident using AI tools.

Another thing I like is that the focus isn't just on teaching ChatGPT or Codex. It's about helping students actually build projects together. Campus Leads receive training, event funding, a ChatGPT subscription, Codex credits, OpenAI swag, a semester stipend, and access to the OpenAI team and a global network of Campus Leads. There are also opportunities to visit OpenAI HQ and connect with other student leaders from around the world.

Program Duration: August 2026 – June 2027

Time Commitment: Approximately 4–6 hours per week

Who can apply: Undergraduate students aged 18 or older who expect to graduate after December 2027. Applicants should be studying in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, India, Japan, or South Korea.

Application Deadline: August 10, 2026 (11:59 PM PT)

📚 Resources Worth Checking Out

Not every useful find comes with an application deadline.

Here's one resource worth checking out this week.

Learning How to Learn (Free Coursera Course)

Who it's for: Students, self-taught developers, career changers, and anyone who wants to become better at learning technical subjects like programming, AI, math, or computer science.

What stands out: Learning How to Learn, taught by Dr. Barbara Oakley and Dr. Terrence Sejnowski, is one of Coursera's most popular courses, with over 4 million learners. Instead of teaching a specific programming language or framework, it focuses on something even more valuable: how to learn effectively. The course covers topics like procrastination, memory, focused and diffuse thinking, chunking, learning strategies, and practical techniques you can apply no matter what you're studying.

I wanted to include this because I genuinely found it helpful. I first came across Barbara Oakley through her TEDx talk, which eventually led me to this course. It completely changed the way I thought about learning difficult subjects. Whether you're learning AI, web development, cybersecurity, or preparing for interviews, I think understanding how to learn is one of the best investments you can make.

One thing I especially wanted to share is that you don't have to pay to take the full course. Coursera has a partner-supported free version that gives you access to all the course content. The only thing you don't receive is the certificate, which I think is a great option if you're primarily there to learn.

Course Length: Approximately 2 weeks (around 10 hours)

Cost: Free (certificate optional)

💡 Free Access Tip: You can take the full version of this course for free (without the certificate). On the Coursera course page, scroll all the way down to the FAQ section. Under More Questions, click Partner-supported free access, then select Learn More followed by Continue to enroll. You'll get access to the complete course content without paying for the certificate.

Format: Self-paced online course

CALEC Volunteer and Internship Opportunities

Back in Edition #6, I featured CALEC's remote volunteer and internship opportunities after Francis (@francistrdev) shared them with the community. If you missed it, you can find the full overview and all the details in Edition #6.

Since sharing this opportunity with the community, Francis has also published a dedicated DEV post about the Full-Stack Developer volunteer role at CALEC. If that role interests you, it's worth checking out for his perspective and some additional information about what the team is looking for.

If I feature it in a future edition, I'll always make sure to credit you. If you discovered it, that recognition belongs to you.

A short description alongside the link makes it much easier for me to review and potentially feature it in a future edition.

💙 Reader Updates

I'm looking forward to this section gradually growing over time, and I'd still love to hear from you.

One of my favorite parts of writing Dev Opportunity Radar has been hearing from people who discovered something they otherwise might have missed.

If you discovered an opportunity through the radar, applied to something, joined a community, attended an event, or simply found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd genuinely love to hear about it.

You don't need to have been accepted or have a big success story to share. Sometimes simply discovering the right opportunity at the right time is already a win.

If you'd like to share an update, feel free to leave a comment on this edition. With your permission, I may feature it in a future 💙 Reader Updates section and tag you so other readers can celebrate your journey too.

I hope this section gradually becomes a place where we can celebrate those stories together, one update at a time.

👋 Until Next Friday

Before I go, I just want to say thank you.

Every week, I spend time searching for opportunities, resources, and communities that I think deserve a little more attention. But one of my favorite parts of this series isn't the research. It's seeing what happens after an edition is published.

Seeing someone discover an opportunity, apply to a program, share a resource, suggest a Community Find, or come back to tell us what they learned reminds me why I started Dev Opportunity Radar in the first place.

The goal has always been simple:

Help people discover opportunities they otherwise might have missed.

Thanks to all of you, it feels like we're doing exactly that.

Whether you've been reading since the very first edition or this is your first time here, thank you for being part of the journey. Every comment, suggestion, and shared opportunity helps make this series better than I could build on my own.

If you ever come across an opportunity, resource, event, community, or anything else you think deserves more attention, I'd love for you to share it in the comments. And if Dev Opportunity Radar helped you discover something exciting, I'd love to hear that too.

Thank you for reading, for sharing, and for helping make this our radar, not just mine.

I'll be back next Friday with more opportunities, resources, and Community Finds.

Until then, take care, and I hope you discover something amazing this week 💙

blocks.html_en: Who it's for: University students, bootcamp graduates, and recent graduates (with less than two years of full-time work experience) who want to gain real-world product, design, or engineering experience while contributing to nonprofit organizations. International students are welcome, and the program is fully remote.

sentences.en: Who it's for: University students, bootcamp graduates, and recent graduates (with less than two years of full-time work experience) who want to gain real-world product, design, or engineering experience while contributing to nonprofit organizations.
sentences.zh: 适合对象：想要在为非营利组织做出贡献的同时获得实际产品、设计或工程经验的大学生、训练营毕业生和应届毕业生（全职工作经验少于两年）。

sentences.en: International students are welcome, and the program is fully remote.
sentences.zh: 欢迎国际学生，该项目完全远程进行。

blocks.html_en: What stands out: Develop for Good matches students with nonprofit organizations to work on real technology projects over a 16-week virtual program. Participants join cross-functional teams alongside designers, engineers, and product managers, receive mentorship from industry professionals, and build products that support causes like education, healthcare, sustainability, poverty alleviation, disaster relief, and more.

sentences.en: What stands out: Develop for Good matches students with nonprofit organizations to work on real technology projects over a 16-week virtual program.
sentences.zh: 亮点：“Develop for Good”将学生与非营利组织相匹配，在为期 16 周的虚拟项目中开展真正的技术项目。

sentences.en: Participants join cross-functional teams alongside designers, engineers, and product managers, receive mentorship from industry professionals, and build products that support causes like education, healthcare, sustainability, poverty alleviation, disaster relief, and more.
sentences.zh: 参与者与设计师、工程师和产品经理一起加入跨职能团队，接受行业专业人士的指导，并开发支持教育、医疗保健、可持续发展、扶贫、救灾等事业的产品。

blocks.html_en: I wanted to include this because one of the biggest challenges early in your career is answering the question, "How do I get experience if every opportunity asks for experience?" Programs like this help bridge that gap. Unlike many volunteer programs, this one is intentionally structured to feel like working on a real product team. Instead of working on another tutorial or personal project, you get to collaborate with a real client, solve real problems, and build something that can become a meaningful portfolio piece.

sentences.en: I wanted to include this because one of the biggest challenges early in your career is answering the question, "How do I get experience if every opportunity asks for experience?"
sentences.zh: 我想把这一点包括在内，因为职业生涯早期最大的挑战之一是回答这个问题：“如果每个机会都需要经验，我如何获得经验？”

sentences.en: Programs like this help bridge that gap.
sentences.zh: 此类计划有助于弥合这一差距。

sentences.en: Unlike many volunteer programs, this one is intentionally structured to feel like working on a real product team.
sentences.zh: 与许多志愿者项目不同，这个项目的结构是故意让人感觉像是在一个真正的产品团队中工作。

sentences.en: Instead of working on another tutorial or personal project, you get to collaborate with a real client, solve real problems, and build something that can become a meaningful portfolio piece.
sentences.zh: 您无需从事另一个教程或个人项目，而是可以与真正的客户合作，解决实际问题，并构建一些可以成为有意义的作品集的东西。

blocks.html_en: Another thing I like is how closely the experience mirrors a real software team. Students work through project planning, stakeholder communication, technical collaboration, documentation, and product delivery over four months. Participants can also receive mentorship, recommendation letters, portfolio case studies, and opportunities to network with professionals during Demo Day. For eligible students from underserved and underrepresented backgrounds, the Develop for Good Fellows program also provides $1,536 unrestricted cash grants upon successful completion.

sentences.en: Another thing I like is how closely the experience mirrors a real software team.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢的另一件事是这种体验与真实的软件团队非常接近。

sentences.en: Students work through project planning, stakeholder communication, technical collaboration, documentation, and product delivery over four months.
sentences.zh: 学生在四个月的时间内完成项目规划、利益相关者沟通、技术协作、文档编制和产品交付。

sentences.en: Participants can also receive mentorship, recommendation letters, portfolio case studies, and opportunities to network with professionals during Demo Day.
sentences.zh: 参与者还可以获得指导、推荐信、作品集案例研究以及在演示日期间与专业人士交流的机会。

sentences.en: For eligible students from underserved and underrepresented backgrounds, the Develop for Good Fellows program also provides $1,536 unrestricted cash grants upon successful completion.
sentences.zh: 对于来自服务不足和代表性不足背景的符合条件的学生，“为优秀研究员而发展”计划还为成功完成后提供 1,536 美元的无限制现金补助。

sentences.en: Program Duration: 16 weeks (Winter 2027 Batch)
sentences.zh: 项目持续时间：16 周（2027 年冬季批次）

sentences.en: Time Commitment: Approximately 5–10 hours per week

📌 发展好冬2027学生志愿者计划

适合对象：想要在为非营利组织做出贡献的同时获得实际产品、设计或工程经验的大学生、训练营毕业生和应届毕业生（全职工作经验少于两年）。 欢迎国际学生，该项目完全远程进行。

亮点：“Develop for Good”将学生与非营利组织相匹配，在为期 16 周的虚拟项目中开展真正的技术项目。 参与者与设计师、工程师和产品经理一起加入跨职能团队，接受行业专业人士的指导，并开发支持教育、医疗保健、可持续发展、扶贫、救灾等事业的产品。

我想把这一点包括在内，因为职业生涯早期最大的挑战之一是回答这个问题：“如果每个机会都需要经验，我如何获得经验？” 此类计划有助于弥合这一差距。 与许多志愿者项目不同，这个项目的结构是故意让人感觉像是在一个真正的产品团队中工作。 您无需从事另一个教程或个人项目，而是可以与真正的客户合作，解决实际问题，并构建一些可以成为有意义的作品集的东西。

我喜欢的另一件事是这种体验与真实的软件团队非常接近。 学生在四个月的时间内完成项目规划、利益相关者沟通、技术协作、文档编制和产品交付。 参与者还可以获得指导、推荐信、作品集案例研究以及在演示日期间与专业人士交流的机会。 对于来自服务不足和代表性不足背景的符合条件的学生，“为优秀研究员而发展”计划还为成功完成后提供 1,536 美元的无限制现金补助。

亮点：全球黑客周：代理是由黑客大联盟 (MLH) 主办的为期一周的免费在线活动，围绕人工智能代理主题，结合了研讨会、技术挑战、社区活动和项目建设。 在一周内，参与者可以参加实时编码会议，按照自己的节奏完成挑战，赚取积分，与 Discord 上的其他构建者联系，并直接向 MLH 社区学习。

我想把这一点包括在内，因为了解人工智能代理变得越来越有价值，但可能很难知道从哪里开始。 该活动通过将指导研讨会与实际挑战相结合，降低了这一障碍，无论您是第一次尝试代理还是希望在现有技能的基础上发展，都可以轻松应对。

我喜欢的另一件事是，您不必承诺在一个周末内构建一个完整的黑客马拉松项目。 相反，您可以参加整个星期，选择您感兴趣的挑战，参加现场会议，并与来自世界各地的数千名开发人员一起学习。 这是培养新技能、结识其他开发人员并在没有传统黑客马拉松压力的情况下保持动力的好方法。

学习如何学习（免费 Coursera 课程）

适合对象：学生、自学成才的开发人员、职业改变者以及任何想要更好地学习编程、人工智能、数学或计算机科学等技术科目的人。

亮点：《学习如何学习》由 Barbara Oakley 博士和 Terrence Sejnowski 博士教授，是 Coursera 最受欢迎的课程之一，拥有超过 400 万学习者。 它不是教授特定的编程语言或框架，而是专注于更有价值的东西：如何有效地学习。 该课程涵盖的主题包括拖延、记忆、集中思维和发散思维、组块、学习策略以及无论你在学习什么内容都可以应用的实用技巧。

我想把它包括在内，因为我真的发现它很有帮助。 我第一次认识 Barbara Oakley 是通过她的 TEDx 演讲，最终引导我学习了这门课程。 它完全改变了我学习困难科目的想法。 无论您是学习人工智能、网络开发、网络安全，还是准备面试，我认为了解如何学习是您可以做出的最佳投资之一。

我特别想分享的一件事是，您无需付费即可学习完整课程。 Coursera 有一个合作伙伴支持的免费版本，让您可以访问所有课程内容。 您唯一没有收到的是证书，如果您主要是为了学习，我认为这是一个不错的选择。
